subproblems.title: Mass-summable series of currents in an open U: the sum is a current with HasSum, mass and support bounds (reused accepted cmcdt_ims_series_current; parent steps 1–5)
subproblems.statement: Assume (VO): for all P, n ∈ ℕ, every U ⊆ ℝ^P, every S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω disjoint from spt S, S(ω) = 0. Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, and X_r ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (r ∈ ℕ) with Σ_r M(X_r) ≠ ∞ (sum in [0, ∞]). Then there is Y ∈ 𝒟_n(U) such that: (i) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) the real series Σ_r X_r(ω) has sum Y(ω) (HasSum); (ii) M(Y) ≤ Σ_r M(X_r); (iii) spt Y ⊆ closure(⋃_r spt X_r). The notions are as follows. 𝒟_n(U) is GeometricCurrentOn U n and 𝒟ⁿ(U) is TestFormOn U n. M(X) = X.mass = M_U(X) is the supremum of ofReal(X(ω)) over ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ 1 for all x. spt X = U ∖ zeroRegion X, where zeroRegion X is the union of the open W with closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U, and X(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W.
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n), Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) S.support → S ω = 0) → ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (X : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsOpen U → ∑' r, (X r).mass ≠ ∞ → ∃ Y : GeometricCurrentOn U n, (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, HasSum (fun r => X r ω) (Y ω)) ∧ Y.mass ≤ ∑' r, (X r).mass ∧ Y.support ⊆ closure (⋃ r, (X r).support)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1–5 of the selected parent proof (evaluation bound, pointwise sum, continuity, mass, support), written for an arbitrary open U and degree n; the parent applies it with U = ℝ^P (univ) and n = k + 1. This is the accepted proof of cmcdt_ims_series_current; the two auxiliary facts it cites (properties of the Euclidean coefficient norm; uniform smallness of null sequences of test forms) are proved inline in steps 1 and 7. Simon Ch. 6, 2.4–2.11, and the M-absolutely convergent series in the proof of 7.2 (chapter-06.txt lines 2117–2124).

Notation. |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_I α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(n)})²)^{1/2}, summed over the finite set 𝓘 of strictly increasing I : Fin n → Fin P; ‖α‖ is the operator norm of the continuous alternating map α. For Z ∈ 𝒟_n(U), M(Z) = Z.mass = Z.massOn U = sup{ofReal Z(ω) : ω admissible}, where ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) is admissible if tsupport ω ⊆ U (true for every test form in U) and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for every x. Write M(Z)^ℝ := M(Z).toReal.

1. (Coefficient norm.) Let c(α) := (α(e_I))_{I∈𝓘} ∈ ℝ^𝓘. The map c is linear and |α| = ‖c(α)‖₂ (Euclidean norm). Hence |α + α'| ≤ |α| + |α'| and |tα| = |t|·|α| for t ∈ ℝ. Since |α(e_I)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_j ‖e_{I(j)}‖ = ‖α‖, we get |α| ≤ C‖α‖ with C := (#𝓘)^{1/2} ≥ 0. In particular c is a bounded linear map, so α ↦ |α| = ‖c(α)‖₂ is continuous.
2. (Bounded coefficient norm.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). The function x ↦ |ω(x)| is continuous (ω is smooth, hence continuous, and step 1 applies) and vanishes outside the compact set tsupport ω, because |0| = 0. So it is bounded; choose c_ω > 0 with |ω(x)| ≤ c_ω for all x.
3. (Evaluation bound.) Let Z ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with M(Z) < ∞, ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), and c > 0 with |ω(x)| ≤ c for all x. Then |Z(ω)| ≤ c·M(Z)^ℝ. Indeed, for s = c⁻¹ and s = −c⁻¹ the form sω lies in 𝒟ⁿ(U) (a submodule), and |sω(x)| = c⁻¹|ω(x)| ≤ 1 by step 1. So sω is admissible and ofReal(Z(sω)) ≤ M(Z) (an admissible value is below the supremum). Since M(Z) < ∞, this means s·Z(ω) = Z(sω) ≤ M(Z)^ℝ. Multiplying the two inequalities by c > 0 gives ±Z(ω) ≤ c·M(Z)^ℝ.
4. (Absolute summability.) Put A := Σ_r M(X_r) < ∞. Every M(X_r) is finite, the real sequence (M(X_r)^ℝ)_r is summable, and Σ_r M(X_r)^ℝ = A^ℝ. For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), steps 2–3 give |X_r(ω)| ≤ c_ω·M(X_r)^ℝ for every r. So Σ_r |X_r(ω)| < ∞, and the real series Σ_r X_r(ω) is summable.
5. (Linear functional.) Put L(ω) := Σ_r X_r(ω). Each X_r is linear and all these series converge, so L(ω + ω') = L(ω) + L(ω') and L(tω) = t·L(ω).
6. (Uniform bound.) If c > 0 and |ω(x)| ≤ c for all x, then |L(ω)| ≤ Σ_r |X_r(ω)| ≤ Σ_r c·M(X_r)^ℝ = c·A^ℝ, by step 3.
7. (Null sequences of test forms are uniformly small.) Let ω_j → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ(U), i.e. TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0: there is a compact K ⊆ U with tsupport ω_j ⊆ K for every j, and for every k the k-th iterated derivatives of ω_j converge to 0 uniformly on K. For k = 0 the iterated derivative of ω_j at x has norm ‖ω_j(x)‖. Hence for every ε > 0 there is j₀ with ‖ω_j(x)‖ ≤ ε for all j ≥ j₀ and x ∈ K; for x ∉ K, ω_j(x) = 0. So ‖ω_j(x)‖ ≤ ε for all j ≥ j₀ and all x ∈ ℝ^P.
8. (Continuity: Y is a current.) A^ℝ ≥ 0. Let ω_j → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ(U) and η > 0, and put ε := η/(2(C + 1)(A^ℝ + 1)) > 0. By step 7, for all large j we have ‖ω_j(x)‖ ≤ ε for every x, hence |ω_j(x)| ≤ C‖ω_j(x)‖ ≤ (C + 1)ε by step 1. Step 6 with c := (C + 1)ε gives |L(ω_j)| ≤ (C + 1)ε·A^ℝ ≤ (C + 1)ε(A^ℝ + 1) = η/2 < η. Hence L(ω_j) → 0. So L is linear and satisfies the sequential continuity condition of GeometricCurrentOn (Simon 6.2.1): there is Y ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with Y(ω) = L(ω) for every ω. By step 4, HasSum (r ↦ X_r(ω)) (Y(ω)) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U); this is conclusion (i).
9. (Mass.) Let ω be admissible. The terms max(X_r(ω), 0) are nonnegative and bounded by |X_r(ω)|, so they are summable, and X_r(ω) ≤ max(X_r(ω), 0). Hence Y(ω) = Σ_r X_r(ω) ≤ Σ_r max(X_r(ω), 0). Therefore ofReal(Y(ω)) ≤ ofReal(Σ_r max(X_r(ω), 0)) = Σ_r ofReal(max(X_r(ω), 0)) (ofReal commutes with nonnegative summable series) = Σ_r ofReal(X_r(ω)) ≤ Σ_r M(X_r), because ω is admissible for every M(X_r). Taking the supremum over admissible ω gives M(Y) ≤ Σ_r M(X_r); this is conclusion (ii).
10. (Support, using (VO).) Let E := closure(⋃_r spt X_r), a closed set, and let x ∈ spt Y; then x ∈ U, since spt Y = U ∖ zeroRegion Y. Suppose x ∉ E. As U is open, U ∖ E is open and contains x; choose ε > 0 with B_ε(x) ⊆ U ∖ E and put W := B_{ε/2}(x). Then W is open, closure W ⊆ closedBall(x, ε/2) ⊆ B_ε(x) ⊆ U ∖ E ⊆ U, and closure W is compact (closed and bounded in ℝ^P). Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W. For each r, spt X_r ⊆ E while tsupport ω ⊆ closure W ⊆ U ∖ E, so tsupport ω and spt X_r are disjoint and (VO) gives X_r(ω) = 0. Hence HasSum (r ↦ X_r(ω)) 0, and by (i) and uniqueness of sums in the Hausdorff space ℝ, Y(ω) = 0. So Y vanishes on W, and W is one of the sets whose union is zeroRegion Y. Then x ∈ W ⊆ zeroRegion Y, contradicting x ∈ spt Y. Therefore spt Y ⊆ E; this is conclusion (iii). ∎
proof_key_steps: |·| is the Euclidean norm of the linear coefficient map, so it is subadditive, homogeneous, continuous and |α| ≤ C‖α‖; every test form has bounded coefficient norm.
Admissibility of ±c⁻¹ω gives |Z(ω)| ≤ c·M(Z) whenever |ω| ≤ c, so Σ_r X_r(ω) converges absolutely for every test form ω.
L(ω) := Σ_r X_r(ω) is linear with |L(ω)| ≤ c·Σ_r M(X_r) when |ω| ≤ c; null sequences of test forms are uniformly small, so L is sequentially continuous: a current Y with HasSum (X_r(ω)) (Y(ω)).
For admissible ω, ofReal(Y(ω)) ≤ Σ_r ofReal(X_r(ω)) ≤ Σ_r M(X_r); taking the supremum, M(Y) ≤ Σ_r M(X_r).
For x ∉ closure ⋃ spt X_r, a small ball W around x has compact closure inside U ∖ closure ⋃ spt X_r; (VO) kills every X_r(ω) with tsupport ω ⊆ W, so Y vanishes on W and x ∉ spt Y.

subproblems.title: A current vanishes on test forms supported away from its support (reused accepted dtc_vanish_off_support; fact (VO))
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P any set, S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n) and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n) with tsupport ω disjoint from spt S, where spt S = U ∖ Z_S and Z_S is the union of all open W with closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U and S(η) = 0 for every η ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport η ⊆ W (GeometricCurrentOn.support). Then S(ω) = 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n), Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) S.support → S ω = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
This is fact (VO) used in step 5 of the selected parent proof, and it discharges the antecedent of the sibling series_current. Source: Simon Ch. 6, 2.11 (definition of spt T, chapter-06.txt lines 297–301); the partition-of-unity argument below is the standard reason why the union in 2.11 is itself a set on which the current vanishes. Notation: "S vanishes on W" means S(η) = 0 for every η ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport η ⊆ W.
1. K := tsupport ω is compact and K ⊆ U, because ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) is a compactly supported smooth form with tsupport ω ⊆ U. If K = ∅ then ω = 0 and S(ω) = 0 by linearity; assume K ≠ ∅.
2. Since K ⊆ U and K ∩ spt S = ∅, we have K ⊆ U ∖ spt S ⊆ Z_S. By compactness there are finitely many open sets W₁,…,W_m from the family defining Z_S (each with S vanishing on W_i) such that K ⊆ W₁ ∪ … ∪ W_m.
3. Take a smooth partition of unity on ℝ^P subordinate to the open cover {W₁,…,W_m, ℝ^P ∖ K} (e.g. Mathlib's SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate for the closed set K and the cover by W₁,…,W_m): smooth ψ₁,…,ψ_m : ℝ^P → [0,1] with tsupport ψ_i ⊆ W_i for each i and Σ_i ψ_i(y) = 1 for every y ∈ K.
4. For each i, ψ_iω (pointwise product of a smooth function and a smooth n-form) is smooth, and tsupport(ψ_iω) ⊆ tsupport ψ_i ∩ tsupport ω ⊆ W_i ∩ K; in particular it is compact and contained in U. Thus ψ_iω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport(ψ_iω) ⊆ W_i, and S(ψ_iω) = 0 since S vanishes on W_i.
5. ω = Σ_i ψ_iω pointwise: if ω(y) ≠ 0 then y ∈ K and Σ_iψ_i(y) = 1; if ω(y) = 0 both sides vanish. By linearity of S, S(ω) = Σ_i S(ψ_iω) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: tsupport ω is a compact subset of U ∖ spt S ⊆ Z_S, hence covered by finitely many open sets W_i on which S vanishes.
A smooth partition of unity (ψ_i) subordinate to this finite cover of K = tsupport ω splits ω = Σ_i ψ_iω into test forms with tsupport(ψ_iω) ⊆ W_i.
Each piece is annihilated by S; linearity gives S(ω) = 0.

subproblems.title: Mass equals weight for integer multiplicity currents on open sets (reused accepted dtc_mass_eq_measure; fact (MM))
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n) and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity representation of T in U (IMRep U n with R.Represents T, i.e. T(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), where Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Then for every open W ⊆ U, M_W(T) = μ_R(W), where M_W(T) = T.massOn W is Simon's mass 6.2.5 with the Euclidean coefficient norm (the supremum of T(ω) over ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y) and μ_R = θHⁿ⌞M = R.measure; both sides are taken in [0, ∞].
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U W : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → IsOpen W → W ⊆ U → R.Represents T → T.massOn W = R.measure W
subproblems.natural_proof:
This is fact (MM) used in step 6(b) of the selected parent proof; the parent applies it with U = W = ℝ^P to get M(X_i) = μ_{R_i}(ℝ^P). Source: Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(3) (chapter-06.txt lines 763–766, stated there without proof) together with 2.4–2.8 (lines 222–283); this is the identity "M_W(S) = μ_S(W) for open W" quoted at the start of the parent proof. Notation: for α ∈ Λⁿ(ℝ^P) (Covector), |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_I α(e_{I(1)},…,e_{I(n)})²)^{1/2}, the sum over strictly increasing I : {1,…,n} → {1,…,P}; e^I ∈ Λⁿ is the covector e^I(v₁,…,vₙ) = det(⟨e_{I(a)}, v_b⟩)_{a,b}; μ := μ_R, so μ(B) = ∫_{M∩B} θ dHⁿ for Borel B. By definition M_W(T) = sup{ofReal T(ω) : ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω(y)| ≤ 1 ∀y} ("admissible" forms).
1. Algebraic lemma. Let τ₁,…,τₙ ∈ ℝ^P be orthonormal, σ ∈ {1, −1}, and let ζ ∈ Λₙ (MultiVector) satisfy ζ(α) = σ·α(τ₁,…,τₙ) for all α. For increasing I put d_I := det(⟨e_{I(a)}, τ_b⟩)_{a,b} = e^I(τ₁,…,τₙ). (a) Expanding each τ_b in the standard basis and using multilinearity and the alternating property (terms with a repeated basis vector vanish, the others are grouped by their increasing rearrangement with the sign of the sorting permutation) gives α(τ₁,…,τₙ) = Σ_I α(e_I)·d_I for every α. (b) By the Cauchy–Binet formula Σ_I d_I² = det(AᵀA), A the P×n matrix with columns τ_b; AᵀA = I_n by orthonormality, so Σ_I d_I² = 1. (c) Hence, by Cauchy–Schwarz, |ζ(α)| = |Σ_I α(e_I)d_I| ≤ |α| for every α. (d) Put α_ζ := Σ_I ζ(e^I)·e^I (a linear function of ζ). Since e^I(e_J) = δ_{IJ} for increasing I, J, α_ζ(e_J) = ζ(e^J) = σd_J, hence |α_ζ| = (Σ_J d_J²)^{1/2} = 1 and ζ(α_ζ) = Σ_I ζ(e^I)² = Σ_I d_I² = 1.
2. By the field `orients` of R there is an Hⁿ-null set Z ⊆ M such that for every x ∈ M ∖ Z, ξ(x) satisfies the hypothesis of step 1 (τ an orthonormal basis of the approximate tangent space T_xM). For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) the function x ↦ θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) is a.e. strongly measurable on M (ξ is, ω is continuous, evaluation is continuous bilinear) and bounded by θ(x)·sup|ω|·1_{tsupport ω}(x) off Z; since tsupport ω is a compact subset of U, ∫_{M∩tsupport ω} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (field `locallyIntegrable_mult`). So T(ω) is the integral of an integrable function.
3. Upper bound. Let ω be admissible. For x ∈ M ∖ Z, step 1(c) and tsupport ω ⊆ W give θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) ≤ θ(x)|ω(x)| ≤ θ(x)·1_W(x). Integrating, T(ω) ≤ ∫_{M∩W} θ dHⁿ = μ(W), so ofReal T(ω) ≤ μ(W). Taking the supremum, M_W(T) ≤ μ(W).
4. Lower bound on a compact set. Let K ⊆ W be compact and 0 < ε < 1. If K = ∅ there is nothing to prove, so assume K ≠ ∅. Fix s > 0 with K₁ := {y : dist(y, K) ≤ s} ⊆ W; K₁ is compact, K₁ ⊆ U, so μ(K₁) < ∞.
 (a) The open sets V_m := {dist(·, K) < 1/m} decrease to K and μ(K₁) < ∞, so for some m with 1/m < s the open set V := V_m satisfies K ⊆ V ⊆ K₁ and μ(V ∖ K) < ε.
 (b) Let α(y) := α_{ξ(y)} (step 1(d)); α is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, so there is a Borel map α̃ : ℝ^P → Λⁿ with α̃ = α μ-a.e. Since θ ≥ 1 on M, μ-null subsets of M are Hⁿ-null; let Z' be a Borel Hⁿ-null set containing Z ∪ ({α̃ ≠ α} ∩ M). For y ∈ M ∖ Z' we have |α̃(y)| = 1 and ξ(y)(α̃(y)) = 1. By Lusin's theorem for the finite Borel measure μ⌞K₁ on ℝ^P (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17; Λⁿ is identified with ℝ^{C(P,n)} through the coefficients α(e_I)) there is a compact F₀ ⊆ K with μ(K ∖ F₀) < ε/2 and α̃|_{F₀} continuous; by inner regularity there is a compact F ⊆ (F₀ ∩ M) ∖ Z' (a Borel set, M being Borel) with μ(((F₀ ∩ M) ∖ Z') ∖ F) < ε/2. As μ(ℝ^P ∖ M) = 0 and μ(Z') = 0, μ(K ∖ F) < ε; moreover F ⊆ M ∖ Z', α̃|_F is continuous, and |α̃| = 1, ξ(·)(α̃(·)) = 1 on F.
 (c) By the Tietze extension theorem (coefficientwise) α̃|_F extends to a continuous β₀ : ℝ^P → Λⁿ. Let r(v) := v / max(1, |v|), the continuous radial retraction of (Λⁿ, |·|) onto its closed unit ball, and β := r ∘ β₀. Then β is continuous, |β| ≤ 1, and β = α̃ on F (because |α̃| = 1 there).
 (d) Let φ_δ be a standard mollifier (smooth, ≥ 0, ∫φ_δ = 1, support in B_δ(0)) and β_δ := β * φ_δ (coefficientwise convolution). Then β_δ is smooth, |β_δ(y)| ≤ ∫|β(y − z)|φ_δ(z) dz ≤ 1 (convexity of the norm, Minkowski's integral inequality), and β_δ → β uniformly on compact sets as δ ↓ 0 (β is uniformly continuous on compact sets). Fix δ with |β_δ − β| ≤ ε on F.
 (e) Choose χ ∈ C_c^∞(V) with 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1 and χ = 1 on K (smooth Urysohn lemma), and set ω := χβ_δ. Then ω is smooth with compact tsupport ⊆ V ⊆ W ⊆ U, so ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), and |ω| ≤ 1: ω is admissible.
 (f) Since χ = 1 on F ⊆ K and ω = 0 off V, T(ω) = ∫_{F} θ ξ(β_δ) dHⁿ + ∫_{M∩(V∖F)} θ χ ξ(β_δ) dHⁿ. For y ∈ F (so y ∈ M ∖ Z'): ξ(y)(β_δ(y)) = ξ(y)(α̃(y)) + ξ(y)(β_δ(y) − β(y)) ≥ 1 − |β_δ(y) − β(y)| ≥ 1 − ε by step 1(c) and (b). For y ∈ (M ∩ (V ∖ F)) ∖ Z, |χ(y)ξ(y)(β_δ(y))| ≤ 1. Since μ(V ∖ F) ≤ μ(V ∖ K) + μ(K ∖ F) < 2ε, we get T(ω) ≥ (1 − ε)μ(F) − 2ε ≥ (1 − ε)(μ(K) − ε) − 2ε ≥ μ(K) − ε(μ(K) + 3).
 (g) Hence M_W(T) ≥ ofReal T(ω) ≥ μ(K) − ε(μ(K) + 3); letting ε ↓ 0 gives M_W(T) ≥ μ(K).
5. Exhaustion. W is open, so W = ⋃_m K_m with the increasing compact sets K_m := {y ∈ W : |y| ≤ m, dist(y, ℝ^P ∖ W) ≥ 1/m} (K_m := {|y| ≤ m} if W = ℝ^P). By continuity of μ from below and step 4, μ(W) = sup_m μ(K_m) ≤ M_W(T). Together with step 3, M_W(T) = μ(W) in [0, ∞]. ∎
proof_key_steps: A unit simple n-vector ζ satisfies |ζ(α)| ≤ |α| (Cauchy–Binet and Cauchy–Schwarz) and has a dual covector α_ζ, linear in ζ, with |α_ζ| = 1 and ζ(α_ζ) = 1.
Upper bound: for every admissible ω, T(ω) ≤ ∫_{M∩W} θ dHⁿ = μ_R(W), so M_W(T) ≤ μ_R(W).
Lower bound on compact K ⊆ W: Lusin, Tietze, radial retraction, mollification and a smooth cutoff give an admissible ω with T(ω) ≥ μ_R(K) − ε(μ_R(K) + 3).
Exhaust the open set W by compact sets to conclude M_W(T) = μ_R(W).

subproblems.title: Simon 3.13 for series: IMReps with finite total weight sum to one IMRep (reused accepted cmcdt_ims_imrep_tsum; parent step 6)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, and R_i = (M_i, θ_i, ξ_i) (i ∈ ℕ) IMReps in U with Σ_i μ_{R_i}(U) < ∞, where μ_R := θ·Hⁿ⌞M is IMRep.measure. Then there is an IMRep R' in U such that for every test form ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) the real series Σ_i R_i.action(ω) has sum R'.action(ω) (HasSum). Here R.action(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHⁿ(x). (An IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) in U is the contract structure IMRep U n: M ⊆ U Borel and countably n-rectifiable; θ : ℝ^P → ℕ measurable, positive on M and locally Hⁿ-integrable on M in U; ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M and, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M, a unit orientation of an approximate tangent space of M at x; Hⁿ = μHE[n].)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : ℕ → IMRep U n), IsOpen U → ∑' i, (R i).measure U ≠ ∞ → ∃ R' : IMRep U n, ∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, HasSum (fun i => (R i).action (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) (R'.action (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Lemma 3.13 and its printed proof (chapter-06.txt lines 897–937), applied to the M-absolutely convergent series of 7.2 (lines 2117–2124) at the level of representations; this is step 6(b)–(e) of the selected parent proof. It is the accepted proof of cmcdt_ims_imrep_tsum. The two constructions it uses, a common orientation of N := ⋃_i M_i and the IMRep of an integer density, are proved below as Lemmas B and C (they are the accepted cmcdt_ims_common_orientation and cmcdt_ims_imrep_of_int_density).
Correspondence with Simon's proof. Along a common orientation η, the partial sums of the integer densities a_i = s_iθ_i1_{M_i} times η are Simon's θ_Nξ_N in (1), up to the sign normalisation ξ_N = ±η. The bound Σ_i ∫|a_i| dHⁿ = Σ_i μ_{R_i}(U) < ∞ gives convergence of these partial sums in L¹(Hⁿ) and Hⁿ-a.e., which is Simon's (2). The limit m is integer valued, and Simon's θ, M_+ and ξ are |m|, N ∩ {m ≠ 0} and sign(m)·η; this is his (3) and the orientation step. Finally, dominated convergence replaces "M_W(T_P − T) → 0" by the identity of the actions, which is all the statement asks.

Notation. μ := Hⁿ = μHE[n]; M_i := R_i.carrier, θ_i := R_i.mult, ξ_i := R_i.orient; A := Σ_i μ_{R_i}(U) < ∞. "ξ orients Q" means IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q: ξ(α) = σ·α(τ₁, …, τₙ) for all n-covectors α, for some orthonormal family τ spanning Q and a fixed σ ∈ {1, −1}.
Two cited facts:
- (TL) Tangent locality: part (a) of the accepted inherited dependency cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub, i.e. (IC)(a) of the parent proof. If U is open and M ⊆ M' ⊆ U are Borel with μ(M' ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, then for μ-a.e. x ∈ M and every subspace Q, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q ⟺ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q.
- (AU) SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique: a set has at most one approximate tangent space at a point.

Lemma A (unit orientations). Let ξ orient Q via (τ, σ).
 (a) ‖ξ‖ ≤ 1 for the operator norm on covectors, because |ξ(α)| = |α(τ₁, …, τₙ)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_b ‖τ_b‖ = ‖α‖.
 (b) If ξ' also orients Q, via (τ', σ'), then ξ' = ξ or ξ' = −ξ. Proof: orthonormal families are linearly independent, and both τ and τ' span Q, so both are orthonormal bases of Q. Hence τ'_b = Σ_a g_{ab}τ_a with g_{ab} = ⟨τ_a, τ'_b⟩. Orthonormality of τ' gives gᵀg = I, so det g = ±1. Multilinearity and the alternating property give α(τ'₁, …, τ'ₙ) = det(g)·α(τ₁, …, τₙ) for every α. So ξ'(α) = σ'σ·det(g)·ξ(α) for all α, with σ'σ·det(g) ∈ {1, −1}. For n = 0 both families are empty, det g = 1, and the same formula holds.

Lemma B (common orientation). Let N := ⋃_i M_i and assume μ(N ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U. Then there are a strongly measurable η : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) and measurable s_i : ℝ^P → {1, −1} with the following two properties. (a) For μ-a.e. x ∈ N there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N x Q such that η(x) orients Q. (b) For every i, ξ_i = s_i·η μ-a.e. on M_i.
 B1. Each M_i is Borel with M_i ⊆ U (IMRep fields), so N is Borel and N ⊆ U.
 B2. ξ_i is a.e. strongly measurable for μ⌞M_i. Let ξ'_i be strongly measurable with ξ'_i = ξ_i μ-a.e. on M_i.
 B3. D_i := M_i ∖ ⋃_{j<i} M_j. The D_i are Borel and pairwise disjoint, D_i ⊆ M_i, and ⋃_i D_i = N.
 B4. η(x) := ξ'_i(x) for x ∈ D_i, and η(x) := 0 for x ∉ N. Then η is strongly measurable. Put g_0 := 0, and let g_{k+1} := ξ'_k on D_k and g_{k+1} := g_k elsewhere. Each g_k is strongly measurable (a piecewise definition over Borel sets). Moreover g_k → η pointwise: g_k(x) = η(x) for k > j if x ∈ D_j, and g_k(x) = 0 = η(x) if x ∉ N. A pointwise limit of strongly measurable maps into the metrizable space Λ_n(ℝ^P) is strongly measurable.
 B5. s_i(x) := 1 if ξ'_i(x) = η(x), and s_i(x) := −1 otherwise. The set {ξ'_i = η} is Borel, being the equality set of two strongly measurable maps into a metrizable space. So s_i is measurable with values ±1.
 B6. Fix j. Apply (TL) with M := M_j ⊆ M' := N ⊆ U. Then for μ-a.e. x ∈ M_j, M_j and N have the same approximate tangent spaces at x. By the IMRep field orients, for μ-a.e. x ∈ M_j there is Q such that M_j has approximate tangent space Q at x and ξ_j(x) orients Q. Also ξ'_j = ξ_j μ-a.e. on M_j. Hence for μ-a.e. x ∈ M_j there is Q_j with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N x Q_j such that ξ'_j(x) orients Q_j. Each M_j is Borel and there are countably many j, so the following holds for μ-a.e. x ∈ N (†): for every j with x ∈ M_j there is such a Q_j.
 B7. Let x ∈ N satisfy (†), and let j be the index with x ∈ D_j. Then x ∈ M_j and η(x) = ξ'_j(x), so η(x) orients Q_j, an approximate tangent space of N at x; this is (a) at x. If x ∈ M_i, then Q_i is also an approximate tangent space of N at x, so Q_i = Q_j by (AU). Lemma A(b) then gives ξ'_i(x) = ±η(x).
 B8. Fix i. Since M_i ⊆ N, μ-a.e. x ∈ M_i satisfies ξ_i(x) = ξ'_i(x) and ξ'_i(x) = ±η(x) (B2, B6, B7). If ξ'_i(x) = η(x), then s_i(x) = 1 and ξ_i(x) = s_i(x)·η(x). Otherwise ξ'_i(x) = −η(x) and s_i(x) = −1, so ξ_i(x) = (−1)·η(x) = s_i(x)·η(x). This is (b).

Lemma C (the IMRep of an integer density). Assume the following.
 - N ⊆ U is Borel and countably n-rectifiable, with μ(N ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U.
 - η is strongly measurable, and for μ-a.e. x ∈ N, η(x) orients some approximate tangent space Q of N at x.
 - m : ℝ^P → ℝ is measurable and integer valued everywhere, with ∫_{N∩K} |m| dμ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U.
Then there is an IMRep R' in U with R'.action(ω) = ∫_N m(x)·η(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for every n-form ω.
 C1. N' := N ∩ {m ≠ 0} is Borel, and N' ⊆ N ⊆ U.
 C2. mult(x) := ⌊|m(x)|⌋₊ ∈ ℕ equals |m(x)|, because m(x) ∈ ℤ. It is measurable, being a monotone function of the measurable |m|, and mult(x) > 0 for x ∈ N'.
 C3. orient(x) := −η(x) if m(x) < 0, and orient(x) := η(x) otherwise. It is strongly measurable: a piecewise combination of η and −η over the Borel set {m < 0}.
 C4. N' ⊆ N is countably n-rectifiable (SimonGMT CountablyRectifiable.mono). For compact K ⊆ U, ∫_{N'∩K} mult dμ ≤ ∫_{N∩K} |m| dμ < ∞.
 C5. Apply (TL) with M := N' ⊆ M' := N. Then for μ-a.e. x ∈ N', N' and N have the same approximate tangent spaces at x. The hypothesis on η holds μ-a.e. on N' ⊆ N. So for μ-a.e. x ∈ N' there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N' x Q such that η(x) orients Q. Then orient(x) = ±η(x) also orients Q: use the same τ and replace σ by −σ if needed.
 C6. C1–C5 verify all fields of IMRep: measurableSet_carrier, carrier_subset, rectifiable, measurable_mult, mult_pos, locallyIntegrable_mult, aestronglyMeasurable_orient and orients. So R' := (N', mult, orient) is an IMRep in U.
 C7. Let ω be any n-form and x ∈ N. If m(x) = 0, then 1_{N'}(x)·mult(x)·orient(x)(ω(x)) = 0 = m(x)·η(x)(ω(x)). If m(x) ≠ 0, then x ∈ N' and mult(x)·orient(x)(ω(x)) = |m(x)|·sign(m(x))·η(x)(ω(x)) = m(x)·η(x)(ω(x)). Hence R'.action(ω) = ∫_{N'} mult·orient(ω) dμ = ∫_N 1_{N'}·mult·orient(ω) dμ = ∫_N m·η(ω) dμ. The last two integrands agree at every point of N, so the integrals over N agree without any integrability assumption.

Main proof.
1. (Masses.) Θ_i := 1_{M_i}·θ_i : ℝ^P → [0, ∞) is measurable. U is open, hence Borel, and M_i ⊆ U, so μ_{R_i}(U) = ∫_{M_i} θ_i dμ = ∫ Θ_i dμ. Θ := Σ_i Θ_i is measurable, and by monotone convergence ∫ Θ dμ = Σ_i ∫ Θ_i dμ = A < ∞.
2. (The union.) N := ⋃_i M_i is Borel, N ⊆ U, and N is countably n-rectifiable (SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_iUnion). Since θ_i ≥ 1 on M_i, μ(N) ≤ Σ_i μ(M_i) ≤ Σ_i ∫_{M_i} θ_i dμ = A. Hence μ(N ∩ K) ≤ A < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U.
3. (Common orientation.) Lemma B applies by step 2. It gives η and s_i with B(a) and B(b).
4. (Integer density.) a_i := 1_{M_i}·s_i·θ_i is real valued and measurable, with |a_i| = Θ_i and a_i(x) ∈ ℤ. Let m(x) := Σ'_i a_i(x), the real tsum, which is 0 when the series is not summable; m is measurable.
 - m(x) ∈ ℤ for every x. If (a_i(x))_i is summable, then a_i(x) → 0, so |a_i(x)| < 1, hence a_i(x) = 0, for all but finitely many i. Then m(x) is a finite sum of integers. Otherwise m(x) = 0.
 - |m(x)| ≤ Σ_i |a_i(x)| = Θ(x) for every x. Hence ∫_{N∩K} |m| dμ ≤ ∫ Θ dμ = A < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U.
5. (The IMRep.) Steps 2–4 (N Borel, countably n-rectifiable and locally Hⁿ-finite; η strongly measurable; m measurable, integer valued and locally integrable on N) and B(a) are the hypotheses of Lemma C for (N, η, m). It gives an IMRep R' in U with R'.action(ω) = ∫_N m·η(ω) dμ for every n-form ω.
6. (Dominated convergence.) Fix ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). It is continuous with compact support, so there is B ≥ 0 with ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ B for all x. The map x ↦ η(x)(ω(x)) is strongly measurable: it is the strongly measurable pair x ↦ (η(x), x) followed by the continuous map (ζ, y) ↦ ζ(ω(y)). By B(a) and Lemma A(a), ‖η(x)‖ ≤ 1 for μ-a.e. x ∈ N, so |η(x)(ω(x))| ≤ B there. On the measure space (ℝ^P, μ⌞N) put F_i := a_i·η(ω) and b_i := B·Θ_i. Then:
 - each F_i is a.e. strongly measurable, and |F_i| ≤ b_i a.e.;
 - ∫ Θ dμ < ∞, so Θ < ∞ μ-a.e.; hence Σ_i b_i(x) < ∞ for a.e. x;
 - x ↦ Σ'_i b_i(x) is measurable and ∫ |Σ'_i b_i| d(μ⌞N) ≤ B·∫ Θ dμ < ∞, so it is integrable;
 - where Θ(x) < ∞, Σ_i a_i(x) converges absolutely, so HasSum (i ↦ F_i(x)) (m(x)·η(x)(ω(x))).
 The dominated convergence theorem for series then gives HasSum (i ↦ ∫_N F_i dμ) (∫_N m·η(ω) dμ).
7. (Identification of the terms.) Fix i. By B(b), θ_i·ξ_i(ω) = s_i·θ_i·η(ω) μ-a.e. on M_i. Using M_i ⊆ N, R_i.action(ω) = ∫_{M_i} θ_i·ξ_i(ω) dμ = ∫_{M_i} s_i·θ_i·η(ω) dμ = ∫_N 1_{M_i}·s_i·θ_i·η(ω) dμ = ∫_N F_i dμ.
8. By steps 5–7, HasSum (i ↦ R_i.action(ω)) (R'.action(ω)) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). ∎
proof_key_steps: μ_{R_i}(U) = ∫ θ_i1_{M_i} dHⁿ, so Θ := Σ_i θ_i1_{M_i} has ∫Θ = A < ∞; N := ⋃_i M_i is Borel, countably n-rectifiable and Hⁿ(N) ≤ A since θ_i ≥ 1 on M_i.

Lemma B (tangent locality (IC)(a), uniqueness of approximate tangent spaces, Lemma A(b)): a strongly measurable η orients the approximate tangent planes of N a.e., and ξ_i = s_iη a.e. on M_i with s_i = ±1.

m := Σ'_i s_iθ_i1_{M_i} is measurable, integer valued everywhere (a summable integer series has finitely many nonzero terms) and |m| ≤ Θ; Lemma C turns (N, m, η) into the IMRep R' = (N ∩ {m ≠ 0}, |m|, sign(m)η) with R'.action(ω) = ∫_N mη(ω) dHⁿ (Simon's θ, M_+, ξ).
With ‖η‖ ≤ 1 a.e. (Lemma A(a)) and ‖ω‖ ≤ B, dominated convergence for series gives HasSum (∫_N 1_{M_i}s_iθ_iη(ω) dHⁿ) (∫_N mη(ω) dHⁿ).
Each term equals R_i.action(ω) because ξ_i = s_iη a.e. on M_i; hence HasSum (R_i.action ω) (R'.action ω).
